end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from where it is grown to home.
Identified local tomatoes as having fewer food miles and likely being fresher.
Explained links between travel distance, fuel use, pollution, freshness, refrigeration and packaging.
Chose the food travelling 10 km as the lower-distance option and explained why.
Comparison of effects on fuel, pollution and freshness was practised; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, identifying where food comes from, and comparing travel distances. They used a clear distance-to-fuel explanation and connected longer travel with pollution, refrigeration and packaging. One comparison of the wider effects still needs practice, and it was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, compare two foods and ask Rohan to name which has fewer food miles and one effect of the difference.
